audit.why: 8.5/10 HARD against a 48.75% win rate is calibrated, and the shipped chart (Renekton 4 / Skill 3) says the right thing: he owns 2-3 and both item stages on paper while 4-6 are even. Full and content agree row for row, so no flip is proposed. Note the chart and the prose disagree in tone at 2+ items — spikes[3] and the late paragraph claim you reclaim the lane outright while win[6] gives it to Renekton. I left the chart alone because the 48.75% win rate does not support handing K'Sante the late game, and flagged the prose instead.

Spike order is right: his level 1-2 point-click window, your level-3 combo, level 6, then his item stages. Dominus and All Out share a 120/100/80 cooldown, so at 6 neither side has an ultimate-uptime edge — the fury bar decides that fight, which the page already says.

audit.whatIsWrong: The lane plan on this page rests on an ability K'Sante does not have. 'You're unstoppable, so his W stun does nothing' / 'bait the W stun with unstoppable W' / 'your unstoppable W eats his W stun' — five separate places. Riot's text for Path Maker is 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes' — reduced damage, not unstoppable, and nothing in the kit says the charge ignores stuns. The exact opposite fact is also missing: empowered Ruthless Predator 'destroys damage shields on the target' and stuns for 1.5 seconds instead of 0.75, which means it deletes your Footwork shield. Separately, 'bait his W-dash' and 'when he dashes in with W' mislabel the dash — W is the double slash and stun at 300 range; the dash is Slice and Dice (E).
audit.why: This is the worst class of error on the site: the page tells a player to walk into a 1.5-second empowered stun on purpose, on the belief that charging W makes them immune to it. Following that instruction loses the fight and probably the lane.
audit.corrected: Path Maker's charge reduces damage taken and stuns on release — it does not grant unstoppable and does not beat Ruthless Predator's stun. Ruthless Predator (W) is 16/14/12/10/8s at 300 range: 0.75s stun normally, 1.5s and shield-destroying above 50 Fury. Slice and Dice (E) is the dash, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. Cull the Meek (Q) heals him every 7 seconds, which is what makes Grievous Wounds timing matter.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is listed in the itemisation block but never tied to a cooldown or a decision.
audit.why: Flagged missing interaction 'needs-antiheal': Cull the Meek is a 7-second heal-on-hit that beats exactly the extended grind K'Sante wants. The timing, not the mention, is what the player needs.
audit.corrected: Written into dosFull[2].d with the real 7s cooldown.

edits.after: Your full kit arrives — Path Maker's charge cuts his burst, then a second Q stack pulls him in and neutralises his dominance.

edits.after: You trade around his fury bar: bait the 16s W stun, step in after it, pull with Q, and your bulk wins the exchange.

edits.before: Renekton owns the first two levels outright — he has a point-click W stun and fury-empowered Q while you have only Ntofo Strikes and no engage at level 1, so don't walk into melee range to last-hit or he'll W-stun you and dump a fury combo. Soak XP from the tip of Q and give up a little CS. The moment you hit 3 and have your full Q-W combo, the lane flips: you can answer his all-in by charging Path Maker (you're unstoppable, so his W stun does nothing) and Q3 to knock him up.
edits.after: Renekton owns the first two levels outright — he has a point-click W stun and a fury-empowered Q while you have only Ntofo Strikes and no engage at level 1, so don't walk into melee range to last-hit or he'll stun you and dump the combo. Soak XP from the tip of Q and give up a little CS. From level 3 your full combo flips it: charge Path Maker to cut the damage of his all-in, stun him back, and pull with your second Q stack. His W is 16s at rank 1 — that gap is your trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a knife-fight around fury. When he dashes in with W expecting a free stun, start charging Path Maker — the unstoppable on W means his stun whiffs and you wall-knock him, then Q3 pulls him in for a clean trade your bulk wins. At 6, All Out is your tipping point: it survives his already-fading burst and converts you into a duelist who out-DPS's a Renekton who's spent his fury. Don't ult into a full-fury Renekton with rage bar up; ult once he's blown his W and Q empower.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a knife-fight around fury. When he dashes in with Slice and Dice expecting a free stun, start charging Path Maker — the charge cuts the damage and the release knocks him into a wall, then your second Q stack pulls him back for a trade your bulk wins. At 6, All Out survives his fading burst and out-damages a Renekton who has spent his fury. Never commit into a full rage bar: empowered Ruthless Predator stuns 1.5s and destroys your Footwork shield outright. Ult after his empower is gone.

edits.after: Bait his 16s W stun, then charge Path Maker into the gap and pull him with your second Q stack

notes: This page carried the most dangerous version of the repo-wide 'unstoppable Path Maker' myth: it was not a stray phrase, it was the stated plan for levels 3 through 6, telling the player to charge W into an empowered 1.5s stun on purpose. The counter-fact — empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields, i.e. your Footwork shield — is in Riot's own text and appeared nowhere. Unresolved tension I did not change: spikes[3] and the late paragraph say K'Sante reclaims the lane outright at 2+ items while win[6]/phases[6] give that stage to Renekton at a 48.75% win rate. One of the two is wrong; see questionsForUser.
